title: Unique identifier in geofencing notifications
description: Geofencing notifications may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user ID) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.

title: Quasi-identifier through location and timing data
description: Combination of location data (zone entry/exit) and timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that uniquely identify individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Identifier in geofencing data
description: The notification may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (child) that enable direct identification.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location and movement patterns (entering/exiting zones) are revealing attributes that can support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive location data collection
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for simple geofencing notifications.

title: Data propagation to external entity
description: Personal data is propagated to the parent (ExternalEntity) where it may be accessible beyond the functional necessity of the geofencing alert.

title: Unawareness of location tracking
description: Data subjects (children) may not be aware that their location is being monitored and notifications are being generated and sent.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed and shared.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location data may exceed what is actually needed for the functional goal of sending arrival/departure notifications.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's location data can be linked to the specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking of the child's movements across contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location with other attributes
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location type, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The Mobile App Backend processes identified location data of the child, which is personal data that directly identifies the child's whereabouts.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's live location data can be linked to a specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking and association of location data with individual identity.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices

title: Profiling an individual through location data
description: Live location data can be analyzed to profile a child's movements, routines, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is collected continuously and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which directly reveals the identity and whereabouts of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data is tied to identifiable individuals

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Live location data contains revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject, including real-time position, movement patterns, and proximity to sensitive locations.
assumptions: Location data reveals sensitive contextual information about the child

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Sharing live location with a secondary guardian may exceed functional necessity.
assumptions: Live location is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Excessive data granularity in location sharing
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level (real-time, continuous tracking) which may be more granular than needed for the stated purpose of guardian access.
assumptions: Guardian access could potentially be satisfied with less granular location data

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated to an external party (Secondary Guardian) where it may be accessible beyond the immediate functional need, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: External entity has access to the shared data

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (Secondary Guardian) which is known at design time, but the exposure to external entities amplifies privacy risk.
assumptions: Secondary Guardian is a known, static party in the system design

title: Unawareness of location data processing by child
description: The child (data subject) may not be fully aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, or may not understand the extent of data collection and disclosure.
assumptions: Child may lack full understanding of data sharing implications

title: Lack of control over location data sharing preferences
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed, shared, and retained by the system.
assumptions: Child has limited ability to customize or control data sharing settings

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing live location data may violate the data minimization principle if more personal data is processed than actually needed for the stated functional goal of guardian access.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this system

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent if the child's consent is not properly obtained, understood, or can be withdrawn.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be insufficient for sensitive location data

title: Data Propagation to External Analytics Partner
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are propagated from the mobile app backend to an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics partner may use this data for purposes beyond funding the free tier, such as building user profiles or selling data.

title: Predetermined External Data Recipient
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) that may not be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party that may have its own data processing policies.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Data subjects (app users) may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with external advertising/analytics partners to fund the free tier.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate this data sharing, or users may not read/understand them.

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Sharing
description: Users lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their usage analytics are shared with external advertising partners.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular consent options for analytics data sharing.

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: More personal data (usage and engagement analytics) is processed and shared than is actually needed to achieve the functional goal of funding the app's free tier.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may contain more detail than necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Potential Invalid Consent for Analytics Sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing for analytics sharing may not rely on valid consent if users are not properly informed or given meaningful choice.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be bundled or not clearly distinguish analytics sharing from core app functionality.

title: Quasi-Identifier Risk in Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement data may contain combinations of attributes that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Aggregation methods may not be sufficiently robust to prevent re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific aggregation techniques used and the granularity of the analytics data.

title: Quasi-Identifiers in Analytics Data
description: The analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., usage patterns, engagement metrics) that are unique to a data subject, making individuals identifiable despite aggregation.
assumptions: Aggregated data may still retain enough detail to identify individuals in small user populations.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the size of the user base and the specific attributes included in the analytics.
